sources.title: MedlinePlus health topics
sources.description: About 1,000 plain-language health topics (conditions, symptoms, tests, wellness) from the U.S. National Library of Medicine.
sources.attribution: Courtesy of MedlinePlus, U.S. National Library of Medicine. NLM does not endorse this collection. General health information, not medical advice.

sources.title: Army First Aid (ATP 4-02.11, 2026)
sources.description: U.S. Army manual for non-medical personnel: bleeding control and tourniquets, airway, breathing, shock, head and eye injuries, burns, fractures and splinting, bites and stings, heat and cold injuries, evacuation.
sources.license: Public domain (U.S. Government work); approved for public release, distribution unlimited.
sources.attribution: ATP 4-02.11, Casualty Response, Tactical Combat Casualty Care, and First Aid, Headquarters, Department of the Army, 23 March 2026. Converted to markdown; figures are not included.

params.name: Army First Aid
params.notice: U.S. Army manual written for soldiers; parts of it assume combat conditions (Tactical Combat Casualty Care). Figures are not included. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.

sources.title: First Aid (Wikibooks)
sources.description: Community-written first aid course: assessment, CPR, bleeding, burns, fractures, environmental emergencies, wilderness and marine first aid.
sources.attribution: Text by Wikibooks contributors, converted to markdown with images and navigation removed.

skip_pages: Appendix D: Notes for First Aid Instructors
params.notice: Community-written and partly outdated (for example, CPR is now 100–120 compressions per minute, and severe limb bleeding is controlled with a tourniquet). Use it for reference, not instead of training with a certified instructor. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
